role: Supplement to existing PR #8 54-source research register and PR #9 editor reference list. Not a claim to have read protected manuscripts.

synthesis.title: The Field of Cloth of Gold
synthesis.relevant_claim: Guînes was English-owned in 1520; Ardres was French; neutral meeting ground between the two. The meeting is no annexation.
synthesis.limitations: The page is not a parcel-scale survey or sixteenth-century cadastral plan.

synthesis.institution: English Heritage Historical Review / Taylor & Francis
synthesis.title: Julian Munby, The Field of Cloth of Gold: Guînes and the Calais Pale Revisited
synthesis.read_scope: Publisher abstract and publicly indexed notes, not complete paywalled article
synthesis.relevant_claim: The historical landscape and fortresses of the Calais Pale can be studied from Tudor surveys and historic maps; no source here gives our inherited 1520s polygon exact status.
synthesis.limitations: TNA E315/371–372 surveying dates to 1556 and the cited Pas-de-Calais CPL 1414 is a much later tracing; neither was directly accessed or copied. Later surveys may not be silently applied to 1520 boundaries.

synthesis.title: Neil Murphy, Tudor England's French Frontier: The Laws of Guînes (1529) and the Defence of the Calais Pale
synthesis.read_scope: University publisher/repository abstract only; embargoed full chapter not examined
synthesis.relevant_claim: 1525 commission for Guînes settlement/security and 1529 legal restrictions/English settler incentives. This does not show measured rural border or law enforcement counts.
synthesis.limitations: No numbers of actually relocated/expelled tenant farmers; no verified parcel or period-specific 1529 GeoJSON.

synthesis.title: Steven G. Ellis, Ireland's English Pale, 1470–1550
synthesis.read_scope: Publisher-hosted extracts and chapter summary, not full book or period-era maps
synthesis.relevant_claim: The English Pale concerned actual restricted administration in parts of four shires; a 1515 reform treatise reported only about half of four medieval shires under king's law. Medieval county limits are not valid Tudor real-control boundaries.
synthesis.limitations: No exact 1520-1529 boundary polygon proved; cannot fill the four modern counties.

synthesis.institution: Irish Historical Studies / Cambridge University Press
synthesis.title: Steven G. Ellis, Prelude to the Tudor conquest: Henry VIII and the Irish expedition of Thomas Howard, earl of Surrey, 1520–22
synthesis.read_scope: Referenced by original investigator as full open-access article; bibliography and record inspected in existing research package
synthesis.relevant_claim: Deputy-led military operations do not demonstrate routine English direct administration over entire Ireland; Monasteroris garrison bounds and retreat need independent original evidence.
synthesis.limitations: Exact garrison footprint and withdrawal date unresolved.

synthesis.institution: Historic Dublin local history / printed 1488-1495 statutes
synthesis.title: The English Pale (transcribed locations and medieval law)
synthesis.read_scope: Later historical transcription/source narrative, not an original 1520-1529 measured border
synthesis.relevant_claim: A 1488 law names a frontier sequence and 1494-1495 action contemplated defensive ditches, but does not prove each segment continuously enforced in 1520s.
synthesis.limitations: Old statute sequence and present-day geocoded place centers must never be treated as current 1520s surveyed control polygon.

synthesis.title: Historic plan of Guînes Castle, Cotton MS Augustus I ii 23
synthesis.read_scope: Reproduction identified by heritage institution; original image not used
synthesis.relevant_claim: A dated landscape/fortification plan exists for research; copying/digitizing its linework requires independent rights and period check.
synthesis.limitations: No historic drawing has been traced/reproduced for this GeoJSON.

synthesis.institution: Love British TV project / historical GIS provenance
synthesis.title: Approved 1497–1519 territorial-footprints research reference layer
synthesis.relevant_claim: Geometries for Calais Pale, Irish Pale and crown-dependent/Scottish islands are pre-existing. Regional hulls represent cited-place enclosures; islands use modern coastal outline.
synthesis.limitations: Historical coastlines not measured; existing geometry should carry forward only as dashed/hatched contextual visualization, no area calculations; source GPL-3.0-or-later applies to derived modern coastlines.

archival_targets.purpose: Reconstruct later survey of Calais Marches as dated comparative evidence. Folio-level source checks required before connecting to 1520s border.
Check provenance of 1876 map copy of an older undated/lost original and reproduction terms; map features not digitized in this task.
Verify Guînes plan date, royal holdings, reuse permission, and what it depicts before digitizing.

drawing_rules: All regional envelopes are historical-geography illustrations with dashed boundaries, never real measured 1520s jurisdiction.
Modern island coastlines may only be contextual extents with hatching/patterned political relation styles, not exact year-1525 measured beaches.
No polygon in this batch can be appended to atlas.colonial_polygons; use standalone dashed reference layer.
Do not infer English control from battle icons in Scotland, France, Ireland or Newfoundland.
Persistent 1519-to-1520 identities and 1529-to-1530 handoff must preserve exact historical temporal status, not erase because of JSON file range.
